text:
[RDSC.5a.8.1] Each backend atom is at most one per
`(schema_name, slot_name, identity_slot_name, atom, window_ns)`
tuple per module ([RDSC.7.2.1]). The runtime must key the state it
allocates on the same tuple.

**The window is part of the key because a declaration may observe
one slot at several of them.** `mean sliding 10_min as recent`
beside `mean sliding 1_h as hourly` selects one backing twice, at
two windows, and each read resolves to its own line's window
([LSER.6.8.1]). One atom per `(schema, slot, identity)` can carry
only one of them, so a key omitting the window answers every read of
that slot from a single window whatever the author wrote.

The atom is part of it for the reason [RDSC.5a.8.2] gives: parallel
backings over one slot are ordinary. No field changes — every backend
atom already carries `window_ns`, and its field number names its backing.
